title: Book Store CRUD with Mongoose
idea: Each Book Store route becomes a Mongoose call on the `Book` model. Mongoose returns promises, so each handler awaits its call.
points: A rejected Mongoose call reaches the error handler; Express 5 forwards it.
`findById` resolves to `null`, not an error, when no document matches.
A malformed id makes `findById` throw, so check it with `isValidObjectId` first.
Send chosen fields; `book.id` is the `_id` as a string.

code.title: The five routes on MongoDB
code.caption: The Book Store on MongoDB. A client replays the requests. Step through it, then press Run.

walk.text: The `Book` model again, inlined so this file runs alone. Both text fields are trimmed.
`show` picks the fields to send, so `__v` stays hidden. `pick` accepts only three fields.
`loadBook` is middleware: a malformed or unknown id gives `404`; otherwise the book goes on `req.book`.
`find` lists, sorted by `year`. `create` saves what `pick` returns, or rejects with a `ValidationError`.
`GET`, `PUT` and `DELETE` share `loadBook`. `set` then `save` re-validates; `deleteOne` removes the document.
The error handler turns a `ValidationError` into `400` with the bad field names; anything else is `500`.
Connect, listen on any free port, then call every route with `fetch`, and close everything.

pitfalls: Never pass `req.body` straight to `create` or `set`; pick the fields you accept.
`PUT` here replaces the whole book: missing fields fail validation, not stay unchanged.
Add `sort` to list queries; without it MongoDB promises no order.

quiz.code:
const id = '66a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b'; // valid format, no such book
console.log(mongoose.isValidObjectId('abc'), await Book.findById(id));
quiz.why: `'abc'` is not a 24-character hex string, so it is invalid. A valid id with no match resolves to `null`.

takeaway: Await each Mongoose call; `null` from `findById` means 404.
